power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

text.text: Background: Traditional psychometrics collapse rich psychedelic experiences into aggregate composite scores, masking the structural dynamics that drive therapeutic outcomes.

Methods: An unsupervised Natural Language Processing framework mapped a substance-specific corpus of psilocybin narrative reports (n = 5,498; ~5.19M tokens) into a continuous seven-dimensional thematic state space, using semantic embeddings and cluster-level differential TF-IDF feature extraction.
Spatial topology metrics, multivariable logistic regression, and substructure analyses characterized its organization, dynamics, and functional roles.

Results: The resulting topology revealed four functional roles across the continuous state space: modulators (e.g., visual patterns, environment, body-object features), a threshold marker (temporal distortion), a peak state (ego dissolution), and a distributed state (unity).
Cognitive-emotional processing emerged as the dominant driver of transitions across this topology, promoting internally-oriented states while suppressing environmental tracking.
Within unity, this topology resolves into two mutually inhibitory pathways: internal cognitive-temporal transcendence and external somatosensory-environmental merging.
Because legacy composite scales like the MEQ30 sum across these opposing channels, feature cancellation masks divergent phenomenological trajectories behind identical composite scores.
Conclusions: Psilocybin phenomenology organizes into a structured, cognitive-emotionally anchored topology rather than unconstrained variation.

Resolving unity into opposing pathways 1 exposes a mechanism of feature cancellation in legacy aggregate psychometrics, whereas the global state-space architecture aligns with neuroimaging evidence of network reorganization and provides a quantitative framework for optimizing dose, set-and-setting, and targeted clinical protocols.
A growing body of clinical research highlights the therapeutic potential of psychedelic-induced subjective altered states of consciousness.
Contemporary evidence demonstrates that long-term clinical efficacy depends directly on the nature and depth of the acute psychological experience itself (Yaden and Griffiths, 2021).

text.text: While molecular neurobiological models suggest that pharmacological agents induce structural circuit repair (Olson, 2021), empirical evidence indicates that the lived subjective experience operates as a primary mediator of transformation in the patient's self-narrative (Letheby, 2021).

text.text: Given the therapeutic role of subjective experience, a topology of its phenomenological architecture is a clinical necessity, without which clinicians cannot reliably leverage experiential patterns to drive therapeutic breakthroughs or prevent psychological distress.

Quantitatively modeling these complex and qualitative experiences remains a significant challenge to standardized psychometric instruments, such as the Mystical Experience Questionnaire (MEQ30; MacLean et al., 2012) or the Altered States of Consciousness Rating Scale (5D-ASC; Studerus et al., 2010), which are commonly applied to gauge the intensity of altered states.

text.text: While useful for baseline correlations, these aggregate scales introduce a systemic measurement challenge, compressing the vast, high-dimensional nature of subjective experience into predefined, low-dimensional scalar summary scores (Van Elk and Yaden, 2022).

text.text: Forcing rich phenomenology into fixed categories risks obscuring the qualitative variations that may drive distinct clinical outcomes and inhibit development of more reliable clinical support systems.

Prior research designs have attempted to navigate these measurement constraints through large-scale surveys and retrospective narrative collections, achieving moderate scale but remaining limited by the predefined architecture of questionnaire formats (Griffiths et al., 2019; Davis et al., 2020; Cox et al., 2021).

text.text: Alternative neuroimaging and qualitative field interview designs seek higher physiological or phenomenological fidelity, yet both approaches are restricted by logistical demands and small sample sizes that limit broad generalizability.

Meta-analytic evaluations reveal that pooled experimental neuroimaging datasets (Dos Santos et al., 2016; McCulloch et al., 2022) and large-scale psychometric trial syntheses (Studerus et al., 2011) often encompass only a few hundred substance-specific (e.g., psilocybin) sessions, while naturalistic qualitative interview studies are typically restricted to fewer than 50 participants (Michael et al., 2023).

text.text: Even when evaluating qualitative narratives, existing analytical frameworks frequently encounter the same data-reduction problem, compressing reports back into the low-dimensional scalar metrics of legacy questionnaires.

While traditional clinical frameworks have historically relied on rigid diagnostic categories or coarse, single-scalar survey metrics, modern computational psychiatry increasingly emphasizes continuous, multidimensional state mapping (Insel et al., 2010).

text.text: However, these efforts predominantly focused on contrasting diverse psychoactive classes (Al-Imam et al., 2025; Ballentine et al., 2022; Noah et al., 2024), necessarily reducing intra-substance variance into class-level averages, obscuring phenomenology specific to individual substances.

text.text: Although inter-class models can isolate specific experiential elements (e.g., differentiating visual terminology), they are blind to intra-session topology, such as how emotional catharsis, somatic load, and spatial altered states correlate within a single experience, remaining inherently unsuited for deep intra-substance mapping.

Because therapeutic application requires a complete, drug-specific profile of the clinical agent, mapping the continuous internal state-space of a single substance represents a crucial unaddressed need in psychedelic research.
In comparison, previous studies isolating single-substance narratives were constrained by sample scale.

Small cohorts, ranging from qualitative sentiment mining to detailed thematic coding on modest datasets (N = 36), lack the statistical power required to construct stable, continuous high-dimensional topologies (Al-Imam et al., 2025; Lawrence et al., 2022).

text.text: The computational framework processes raw narrative corpora in a multi-stage pipeline designed to map qualitative text into a structured, continuous state space.
First, narrative reports undergo standard text preprocessing before transformation into high-dimensional vector representations using dense transformer embedding models.

These high-dimensional text embeddings are then refined through clustering to reveal stable dimensions of thematic grouping, representing each experience report not by a single label, but as a data point in a continuous mixture space where a narrative retains fractional membership across seven discovered themes (e.g., partitioning an individual experience across explicit ratios of, say, ego dissolution, visual patterns, or body features).

To visualize this multi-dimensional mixture data without losing its inherent properties, the framework applies the Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) algorithm (McInnes et al., 2018) to compress the high-dimensional thematic vectors into an interpretable 2D geometry.

text.text: Combining text embeddings, unsupervised clustering, non-linear geometric mapping, and predictive models, the framework establishes a computational foundation that maps both the static structures of the altered state, and the directional trajectories inherent in the phenomenology.

To build a foundational dataset of acute psilocybin experiences, the data utilized in this analysis were obtained from the Erowid Experience Vaults online repository (Erowid Center, 2026) according to the platform's automated access guidelines.

text.text: Two different datasets, one comprising 40,254 user reports across multiple substances (including non-psychedelic), and another, 7655 psilocybin-specific reports, were merged and filtered down to a corpus of 10,979 unconstrained narratives of psilocybin experiences (of which 93 were removed as duplicates).
Raw self-reports frequently involve poly-substance combinations or extensive non-phenomenological context.

To ensure the downstream analysis reflects pure psilocybin dynamics, a Llama 3.3 (70B) large language model (Grattafiori et al., 2024) was deployed to partition this combined dataset (N = 10,979) into subsets of strictly-psilocybin use (n = 5,498, precision 96%, recall 79%), those mixed with other hallucinogens (n = 2,053, precision ~100%, recall ~100%), and those co-experienced with cannabis (n = 3,357, precision 40%, recall 80%), with 71 reports deemed inconclusive.

text.text: Classification accuracy was manually evaluated on random samples of 250 instances per class.

Filtering out cross-substance information (both the mixed with cannabis and other hallucinogenic datasets were discarded), yielding 5,498 strictly-psilocybin experiences (comprising 5,191,050 total tokens, with a mean length of ~944 tokens per report), represents a high-confidence dataset that is specifically suitable for tracking the topology of a single chemical family by avoiding the compound blurring that is typical of multi-substance content.
Prior to vectorization, the Llama 3.3 (70B) architecture was further utilized to apply extractive semantic filtering to each report.

This isolated the core phenomenological text while systematically removing non-experiential noise, after which the text was transformed into a 384-dimensional embedding vector representation, using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Sentence Transformer, to quantitatively capture the semantics and tone for each experiential content in vector format.

Exploring the empirical distribution of the corpus revealed key structural properties that guided downstream feature engineering, establishing a continuous seven-dimensional state-space as a foundational topology.
Revealing the composite nature of experience.

Having projected each narrative into a 384-dimensional dense vector space ( ), exploratory iterative K-means clustering was ℝ 384 applied to evaluate the compositional structure of acute psilocybin narratives.

Progressively increasing the cluster parameter from K = 2 to K = 10 revealed that the data do not cleanly separate into discrete, isolated partitions; rather, embedding vectors occupy a continuous space characterized by peripheral overlap and spatial interpenetration between neighboring domains (see Figure 3 in Results).

text.text: This lack of clear spatial separation indicates that hard-clustering artificially divides what is fundamentally a shared mixture of co-occurring phenomenological states.
To identify distinguishing thematic signatures, statistical feature extraction was paired with qualitative synthesis across multiple cluster resolutions.

text.text: Having established experiences as mixtures of themes, the framework investigates this seven-dimensional phenomenological landscape by leveraging three distinct methodological approaches: 1.
Geometric analysis: visualizing the spatial architecture of the phenomenological landscape.
Quantitative measurement: applying formal statistical metrics calculations.
Modeling: rationalizing and explaining thematic behavior.
To visualize the structural landscape, UMAP was applied to compress the seven-dimensional feature space into a two-dimensional projection.

This non-linear dimensionality reduction is uniquely suited for preserving the inherent topology of the data across three distinct scales, maintaining: (1) Local neighborhoods: such that if two reports are similar in 7D theme membership they remain close in a 2D geometry.
(2) Global structure: keeping the broader relationships between different thematic regions.
(3) Manifold continuity: preserving a topology that assumes locally continuous data.
Within this 2D space, three geometric and distributional properties were evaluated: • Thematic centroids: representing the mathematical spatial center of mass for each individual theme.
The centroids reflect the concentration point where narratives heavily dominated by a specific theme naturally cluster.
• Dominant theme distribution: mapping the locations of reports where a given theme exhibits the highest relative intensity vector.
This highlights the localized spatial dominance of individual themes across the manifold.

• Mean-deviation gradients: capturing the gradual variance of each dimension across the topology by measuring how much a narrative's thematic score elevates (positive deviation) or is suppressed (negative deviation) relative to its dataset-wide mean.
This normalization converts raw intensity metrics into a spatial map of localized phenomenological highlights.

Mapping acute psilocybin experiences across three complementary spatial resolutions-384D sentence embeddings, 7D thematic coordinates, and 2D manifold projections-resolves the global state-space into a continuous, multi-level topology.
Across scales, cognitive-emotional processing emerges as a primary system-wide driver, with vector dynamics reflecting distinct divergent trajectories within unitive states.
Quantifying these multi-resolution dynamics establishes empirical parameters to track state transitions, exposes limitations in static psychometrics, and informs target selection for clinical trials.
An exploratory investigation into the syntactic nature of reported phenomenology was conducted across a refined corpus of psilocybin narratives (n = 5,498; ~5.19M tokens).

Clustering of embedding vector representations (384D) of these reports revealed that experiences do not naturally partition into fixed discrete clusters but form an overlapping mixture space with interpenetration between neighboring domains, suggesting that psilocybin experiences typically involve multiple co-occurring thematic dimensions rather than isolated, mutually exclusive experiential types (Figure 3).

This work establishes a computational framework for extracting clinically useful patterns relevant to the psilocybin experience, demonstrating that the apparent complexity and heterogeneity of qualitative trip reports can be organized into a structured topology.
Three findings emerge with direct clinical and methodological significance.

First, global state transitions across this topology are systematically mediated by cognitive-emotional processing, which functions as a primary predictive driver guiding trajectories across the manifold.

Second, topological decomposition reveals that unitive phenomena are not monolithic, but split into two distinct channels: an internal pathway (cognitive-temporal transcendence) and an outward pathway (somatosensory-environmental merging).
Third, these channels exhibit strong reciprocal inhibition, demonstrating that aggregated psychometric scores can mask opposing experience dynamics.

Together, these results advance psychedelic research from simple categorization toward an actionable, high-resolution geometry of experiential consciousness, establishing a data-driven foundation for refining therapeutic protocols.
Multiple lines of evidence converge to identify cognitive-emotional processing as the primary driver of state dynamics across the manifold.
In 2D state-space projections, this domain occupies a central region that directly overlaps with internally oriented themes.
In 7D spatial analyses, it demonstrates unique global density and modulatory prominence.

Finally, multivariable regression confirms its role as a primary statistical driver, simultaneously co-elevating with internally oriented states (temporal distortion, ego dissolution, and unitive processing) while downregulating externally focused environmental tracking.

Rather than emerging from unstructured narrative entropy, these state transitions operate under systematic topological principles-a finding that echoes recent population-level neuroimaging showing organized neural remapping under psilocybin across varying contexts (Stoliker et al., 2026).

text.text: These two trajectories closely parallel the distinction between introvertive and extrovertive mysticism proposed by Stace (1960), who described introvertive unity as an inward-turning experience in which the sense of self, sensory content, time and space dissolve, and extrovertive unity as an outward-facing apprehension of oneness perceived through the senses in the external world.

text.text: The internal pole identified here, defined by ego dissolution, time distortion and cognitive-emotional processing, corresponds to the former; the outward pole, defined by environmental, visual and somatosensory features, corresponds to the latter.

This correspondence emerged from unsupervised analysis of naturalistic narratives, without reference to Stace's framework or any questionnaire structure, providing independent, data-driven support for a distinction that has largely rested on philosophical analysis and factor analyses of questionnaire items (Hood, 1975; Hood et al., 2001).

text.text: The present findings also refine it: rather than two discrete types, introvertive and extrovertive unity form opposing poles of a single continuous manifold (K = 1), linked through a baseline unitive region and expressed in graded mixtures.
This structure has a direct consequence for the MEQ30.

These findings therefore reframe a long-standing debate over whether unitive states constitute a single construct (MacLean et al., 2012; Barrett et al., 2015) or discrete categorical types (Griffiths et al., 2006): unitive experience appears to be neither, but a continuous landscape organized along an inward-outward axis.

text.text: The most immediate clinical implication concerns measurement.
If composite instruments sum across inversely related experiential channels, then patients with matched composite scores may differ systematically in their underlying trajectories.

This generates a directly testable prediction: in existing trial datasets with item-level MEQ30 or 5D-ASC data, participants with matched totals but divergent inward versus outward profiles should show different therapeutic outcomes.
In parallel, the present pipeline can score written post-session reports, which many trials already collect, on the same seven dimensions, providing a complement to questionnaire-based measures.

Translating the above topological mechanisms into clinical practice provides a framework for real-time state navigation, trial design, and protocol optimization, utilizing predictive models to anticipate individual treatment trajectories (Feuerriegel et al., 2024).

text.text: Viewing altered states as traversable trajectories through a structured landscape implies that experiences follow probabilistic transition dynamics rather than arbitrary fluctuations.
Within this framework, particular feature dynamics could function as real-time state-transition markers.

For instance, a participant's report of temporal slowing may indicate that the session has crossed the threshold marked by time distortion, a region of the state space closely associated with ego dissolution in the present data.

Furthermore, because ego dissolution is a highly localized boundary state, future trials could test whether doses sufficient to cross this threshold occasion ego dissolution more reliably than lower doses.
Moreover, the central topological role of cognitive-emotional processing provides an operational lever for steering session dynamics and engineering set-and-setting protocols.

Because internal dimensions interconnect directly through this central core, modulating the participant's pre-dosing cognitive-emotional set via targeted preparation, therapist grounding, or curated music selection allows clinicians to guide overall manifold trajectories, while acute cognitive-emotional destabilization serves as an early-warning marker for emerging distress.
Crucially, disaggregating monolithic unitive states into bipolar experiential channels enables trajectory-targeted protocol design.

Internal unitive trajectories (cognitive-temporal transcendence) represent the primary target vector for internalized affective conditions such as Major Depressive Disorder, where disrupting rigid self-referential narratives is essential (Carhart-Harris et al., 2016).

text.text: Together, stratifying patients by these distinct topological trajectories transforms psychedelic administration into a precision-guided intervention capable of tailoring set, setting, and therapeutic support to targeted experiential states.
Several methodological and observational bounds warrant consideration when interpreting these findings.

At the observational level, constructing state-space coordinates from crowdsourced natural language reports introduces inherent recall bias, selective self-reporting, and post-hoc narrative smoothing (Mooseder et al., 2022).

text.text: At the analytical level, natural language embeddings serve as a conceptual proxy for underlying neurological activity.

Although semantic term frequencies map subjective feature co-occurrence with high resolution, language captures the cognitive and narrative representation of an altered state rather than direct, real-time physiological or cortical dynamics.

Methodologically, deriving report-level coordinates via normalized term frequencies relies on simplifying assumptions: unweighted summation assumes equal semantic contribution across cluster terms, whereas exact keyword matching fails to account for polysemous or context-dependent usage.

Future refinements should incorporate dynamic, token-level contextual embeddings (e.g., transformer-based attention masks) to assign fractional thematic membership based on immediate syntactic context.

Nevertheless, aggregating normalized term frequencies into multidimensional coordinates provides a transparent, interpretable framework for mapping the continuous topology of experience directly from unconstrained natural language reports.

A geometric manifold framework is uniquely suited for such naturalistic corpora: rather than fitting global parametric functions across skewed sample distributions or forcing linear correlations on unobserved confounders, it projects noisy inputs into localized spatial coordinates that reveal continuous state relationships.

Demonstrating exceptional statistical robustness, the directional stability observed across all primary multivariable models, reinforced by non-parametric bootstrapping and cross-stage alignment across two-dimensional observations, seven-dimensional spatial statistics, and predictive modeling, confirms that this state-space topology recovers reproducible phenomenological signals rather than fitting noise within crowdsourced data distributions.
Without relying on rigid survey priors or supervised target labels, this framework autonomously recovers the foundational feature space of psychedelic phenomenology.

Moreover, while the seven-dimensional coordinate system was specifically selected to capture system-wide patterns across psychedelic experiences, the underlying framework is fundamentally dimensional-agnostic.

This architecture establishes a generalizable computational paradigm for converting unconstrained and unstructured qualitative reports into quantitative topologies-a scalable system for uncovering state-space patterns by projecting narratives into spatial coordinates over an adaptable number of dimensions.

Consequently, the architecture extends beyond psilocybin or specific psychedelic states, offering a methodology for mapping reports across diverse altered states of consciousness, pharmacological interventions, and psychiatric phenomena.

The study enables algorithmic resolution into the internal dynamics of the acute psilocybin state, exposing continuous state-space trajectories and low-amplitude phenomenological features that are routinely erased when forcing diverse pharmacologies into a shared comparative framework.

Because clinical trials test specific compounds rather than generic psychedelics, a single-substance state space provides the baseline needed to track patient trajectories, state transitions, and dose-dependent effects.

Integrating text embeddings, unsupervised clustering, and predictive regression modeling yields a robust seven-dimensional state-space topology that isolates reproducible phenomenological signals from narrative noise and unobserved set-and-setting confounders, delivering five distinct primary contributions to psychedelic research: (1) discovery of continuous experiential topology, uncovering the intrinsic geometry of the psilocybin landscape across seven stable feature dimensions to establish a functional hierarchy of continuous modulators, state-dependent threshold markers, and peak sub-regions; (2) deconstruction of monolithic unity, demonstrating that unitive experiences do not form a single homogeneous phenomenon, but fundamentally split into two primary paths dividing internal cognitive-temporal transcendence from external somatic-environmental embodiment; (3) quantitative evidence for psychometric scale cancellation, addressing a key limitation in clinical literature by showing that legacy summary metrics suffer from severe feature cancellation when aggregating mutually inhibitory experiential channels; (4) framework for targeted therapy, identifying a centralized state space driven by a cognitive-emotional core to establish quantitative parameters for navigating system dynamics and engineering targeted clinical set-and-setting; and (5) neurobiological alignment, establishing a conceptual bridge between phenomenological state space and neuroimaging research by demonstrating how this topological framework complements models of cortical entropy, showing that phenomenological state dynamics remain systematically structured despite neural desynchronization, while contextualizing somatic constraints within predictive processing frameworks.
Together, these contributions advance psychedelic research from coarse scalar metrics toward a predictive, high-resolution geometry of human consciousness.

Driven by these selective state dynamics, unitive phenomena inevitably split into two distinct topological trajectories rather than forming a single, uniform state.

This structural bifurcation exposes the fundamental limitations of legacy psychometric instruments, explaining score equifinality, wherein different individuals achieve identical high composite scores through distinct experiential pathways.

Standard measurement tools, such as the Mysticism Scale and the 30-item Mystical Experience Questionnaire (MEQ30), evaluate unitive phenomena by summing diverse subjective items into a single summary metric.

However, topological decomposition demonstrates that high unitive ratings arise through two distinct phenomenological trajectories: an internal unity pathway characterized by elevated cognitive processing intensity, ego dissolution, and the distortion of temporal flow, and an outward pathway defined by somatic embodiment, sensory synthesis, and environmental merging.

Because internal dimensions, including ego dissolution, temporal distortion, and cognitive-emotional processing, operate under strong mutual inhibition with external environmental grounding and sensory streams, aggregating these divergent dimensions into a single composite score causes opposing dimensional subscores to cancel each other out.
